assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory established that collective motion is a genuine non-equilibrium phase of matter with long-range order in two dimensions, in defiance of the Mermin-Wagner intuition, and with universal scaling exponents. This is the kind of simple, general mechanism behind a messy multi-scale phenomenon that I find most compelling, and it has reshaped soft matter, biological physics and machine-learning-adjacent work on active matter.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal numerical model in 1995; Toner and Tu supplied the continuum theory and the renormalisation-group argument for long-range order. These three contributions are distinct and complementary, so the three credited names map cleanly onto a fair prize configuration. Other contributors to active-matter hydrodynamics (e.g. Ramaswamy, Marchetti) are not credited here and the boundary of the field's credit is somewhat open.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of theory, simulation, and confirmation in colloidal rollers, bacterial suspensions and vibrated granular systems. Giant number fluctuations and the exponents have been tested, though quantitative agreement of exponents in experiments is partial. Recognition is timely and the field is stable.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation of the specific Toner-Tu exponents is less clean than the qualitative phase-transition picture.
Credit might be argued to extend to others in active-matter hydrodynamics beyond the three listed names.
I have not independently verified details of the experimental literature; this relies on my general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological classification, together with the HgTe/CdTe experimental realisation, opened the field of topological insulators and symmetry-protected topological matter. It is a clean, general, rigorously analysed idea with a decisive experimental confirmation, and its influence on condensed-matter physics has been enormous.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical contribution; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation (2007) following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. BHZ (Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes) are not in the credited names, which creates an unresolved credit question for the HgTe prediction. Haldane's earlier Nobel (2016) covers the topological precursors, which helps a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp configuration but leaves some tension.
assessment.maturity: Well over fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, InAs/GaSb, 3D topological insulators and photoemission, with stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the credited names leaves the HgTe prediction credit unresolved.
The overlap with the 2016 prize may lead some members to view this as already partly recognised.
Whether the prize should be theory-led or split theory and experiment differently is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller laid the theoretical foundations for trapped-ion quantum gates and for analogue quantum simulation with cold atoms in optical lattices, creating blueprints that became experimental programmes worldwide. The originality and lasting impact on quantum information and many-body physics are very high.
assessment.attribution: A two-person prize is natural and the credit is comparatively clear: the 1995 ion-trap gate proposal and the 1998 Hubbard-model-in-lattice proposal (with Jaksch et al.) are overwhelmingly associated with these two. Experimental realisation credit (Blatt, Wineland, Bloch, Greiner) lies elsewhere and partly in earlier prizes (Wineland 2012).
assessment.maturity: Ion-trap quantum computing and optical-lattice simulation are fully mature and independently demonstrated by multiple groups. Recognition would be timely, with the 2025 circuit prize showing the committee's recent interest in quantum-information hardware.
uncertainties: Overlap with other ballot candidates on lattice simulation (Bloch, Greiner) and ion computing (Blatt) could complicate how a theory-only prize is framed.
Wineland's 2012 prize may lead some to consider ion-trap work partly recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture from Liu and Nagel unified granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses under a single phase-diagram concept, and later work on the jamming point as a critical point with isostaticity and universal scaling exponents gave a sharp mechanism for rigidity in disordered matter. It is exactly the type of general, analysable idea I value, tied closely to experiment.
assessment.attribution: The 1998 Liu-Nagel proposal is clearly attributable to the two credited names. The later critical-point theory (O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Parisi and collaborators) is not credited and means the 'jamming as critical phenomenon' result has a distributed origin, but the founding concept is theirs.
assessment.maturity: Well-studied for over twenty-five years, with experimental tests in emulsions, colloids and granular systems. However, some aspects of the theory (relation to the glass transition, nature of the critical point) remain debated, so the interpretation is not entirely settled.
uncertainties: The upper-critical-dimension and mean-field picture of jamming is still debated, and the connection with glass physics is incomplete.
Parisi's 2021 prize on disordered systems partly overlaps in themes; some members may see the field as already honoured.
Distributed credit for the quantitative critical-point theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's realisation of clocks at the 10^-18 level have redefined the precision of timekeeping, opening tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a pathway to redefining the second. The impact is clear, quantitative and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the optical lattice clock concept (2001-2003) and Ye led the strontium clocks that reached record accuracy; both are plainly decisive. Hall and Hänsch's frequency-comb work, already recognised in 2005, and Ludlow, Schmidt, Wineland (Al+ clock) are adjacent contributors. A two-person prize is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and improved the clocks, and comparisons between them are routine. Timing is good, especially if the redefinition of the second is approaching.
uncertainties: Credit relative to ion clocks (Wineland group, Al+ clocks) and the comb prize of 2005 is a possible point of dispute.
Whether the committee prefers a prize in precision metrology this soon after other AMO prizes is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is one of the cleanest examples of a non-equilibrium universality class, with exact solutions linking it to random-matrix theory (Tracy-Widom distributions) and a striking experimental test in liquid-crystal turbulence. It satisfies my preference for universal mechanisms with rigorous analysis and links to random-matrix theory, a field I know well.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 paper is by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang; Parisi has already received the 2021 prize for other work, which complicates re-crediting him. Exact solutions (Johansson, Prähofer-Spohn, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) are mathematical contributions not listed. Including Takeuchi as experimental confirmer gives a mixed theory-plus-experiment configuration that is reasonable but not uncontroversial.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in turbulent liquid crystals (2010-2012) is strong but is essentially a single group's platform plus a few others; the broader relevance to other physical systems is still being established. Timing is plausible, though some members could see it as somewhat premature or more a mathematical than physical prize.
uncertainties: Parisi is a co-author of the original paper and a 2021 laureate; credit allocation for the 1986 result is awkward.
Experimental confirmation is limited in scope and breadth of independent platforms.
Much of the deepest progress is mathematical, and lies outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the final missing particle of the Standard Model, a landmark that required extraordinary instrumentation, analysis and collaboration. The scientific significance is unquestionable, and the Higgs mechanism itself was recognised in 2013.
assessment.attribution: The experimental discovery is a collaboration of several thousand people, and the Nobel statutes allow at most three laureates and no organisations. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at discovery), Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson) and Virdee (CMS) represent leadership, but CMS spokesperson at the time (Incandela), Della Negra and others have comparable claims. Any choice is partly arbitrary and the allocation of credit is the principal obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed, with couplings measured and independent verification from both experiments. Recognition is mature; the main question is whether it is still to be rewarded given the 2013 theory prize.
uncertainties: No unambiguous fair three-person configuration exists for a collaboration of this size, and the proposed set is one defensible choice among several.
My own research is far from particle physics, so my weighting relies on general knowledge of the discovery history.
Whether the committee regards the 2013 prize as having already closed the topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave window, probing supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic early-universe sources. The Hellings-Downs correlation signature makes the measurement conceptually clean, and the technique extends the 2017 prize's field to a new frequency band.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from independent collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA), and the credited names cover pioneers of pulsar-timing infrastructure rather than a single decisive discovery. Kramer (EPTA), Manchester (PPTA) and McLaughlin (NANOGrav) span three major arrays; Siemens, also credited, is equally plausible. Detection significance and sources of credit are still shared across large teams.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is around 3-4 sigma in several arrays, with no individual claim of a firm discovery; the origin (astrophysical versus cosmological) is not settled. Recognition now would be premature relative to more mature candidates, so it ranks last of my eight.
uncertainties: Detection significance is below the conventional discovery threshold in each array.
The physical origin of the signal is unresolved.
Credit is spread across several collaborations and decades of timing work, so any three-person selection is contestable.
